dedupe_keys.name: breitbandatlas austria fixed and mobile broadband availability and subsidised roll out

description: The Breitbandatlas is the Austrian federal government's central platform on broadband availability. Its maps show the fixed and mobile broadband networks available across Austria, the internet service providers from which fixed-line access products can be bought, and the areas where subsidised roll-out of fixed access networks is taking place under the government's Breitband Austria 2020 and Breitband Austria 2030 programmes; for mobile networks it adds analyses of results from the regulator's RTR-NetTest to indicate the average speeds users actually achieved in each network. The broadband office publishes the raw data behind the maps as open data on data.gv.at: quarterly fixed-network availability and mobile-network availability files (the latest at the time of reading were for the first quarter of 2026, released on 10 August 2026) in CSV and Parquet, and the subsidised roll-out areas as a GeoPackage (second quarter of 2026), plus the unfiltered map layers as a WMTS service and pop-up information through GetFeatureInfo requests. Coverage: Austria, quarterly. Format and access: CSV and Parquet in zip archives (the fixed-network file is about 7.4 MB), GeoPackage, WMTS, free under Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Austria. Caveats: availability is reported by operators and may overstate real service; mobile availability is modelled; subsidy areas show planned or ongoing works. Simulation uses: service coverage and redundancy for resilience studies, targeting of backup connectivity, and the progress of planned fibre roll-out. Related records: RTR-NetTest supplies the measured speeds, and the German Breitbandatlas and Swiss BAKOM atlas are the neighbouring counterparts.
